function re-checks session and step-up inside its body (class:line), and `dumpsys` shows no function
beyond the inventory — record the table.

items.title: On-device model file replaceable through a write primitive or stored on external storage — substitution flips the verdict
items.severity_note: High when the model decides something the server trusts (liveness, fraud, document authenticity, moderation); Medium for a classifier that only shapes UI
items.vrt: `ai_application_security.adversarial_example_injection.ai_misclassification_attacks` (P4) as the vector; the sink's node — `broken_authentication_and_session_management.authentication_bypass` (P1) for a KYC/liveness verdict (D13-081) — sets the priority

Locate where the model is loaded from at runtime (asset, `files/`, `cache/`, external
storage, OBB) and who can write there (D11-001's reader/writer rule). If a non-root path exists,
substitute a model whose output is constant (same input/output tensors) and show the verdict the

```bash
frida -D "$SERIAL" -n "$PKG" -l frida/06-file-trace.js -t 5 | grep -iE '\.(tflite|task|onnx|ort|gguf|pte|bin)$' | tee -a logs/D28-038.txt   # the real load path
adb -s "$SERIAL" shell 'ls -la /sdcard/Android/data/'"$PKG"'/files /sdcard/Android/obb/'"$PKG" 2>/dev/null
# build the constant model with the same signature (tflite: a tiny graph that returns the "pass" tensor); drop it through the primitive; re-run the flow
```

The Frida trace showing the substituted file path loaded, the flow accepting (liveness
"pass", fraud score 0) and the server accepting the result (D28-044's proof), with the write
performed by the probe app or the no-root primitive.
items.escalation:
→ D13-081 for the KYC/liveness consequence at P1; → D28-044 when the server trusts the
verdict regardless of the model; → D17-008 when the "model" directory also takes code.
items.ruled_out_when:

`/data/user/0/<pkg>/…` or an asset fd), no other UID can write it (D11-001), and the server re-scores
(D28-044 n/a) — record the load path and the writer analysis.

items.title: Client-side safety or moderation only — the on-device classifier gates an upload or a message and the server trusts the client's verdict
items.severity_note: Medium; High where the bypassed control is a platform-policy or legal gate (CSAM/abuse filters, age gates) and the programme pays for abuse-prevention bypass — read its rules
items.vrt: `broken_access_control.privilege_escalation` (varies) — the control bypassed decides; `ai_application_security.adversarial_example_injection.ai_misclassification_attacks` (P4) when the bypass is an adversarial input rather than a hook
items.attacker: AM-12 to flip the verdict (own device); the finding is the server's trust — rate it as AM-01 (the verdict field from curl) when the verdict travels in the request
items.applies_to: Apps running a moderation/safety classifier on the client before an upload, post or message
items.maps_to: D23-005 (two-half rule), D15-082 (status asserted by the client); MASWE-0050; CWE-602, CWE-807
items.skip_when: `grep -rlE 'moderation|safety|nsfw|toxic|classif' "$DEC/jadx/sources" | grep -viE 'androidx|kotlin' | wc -l` is 0; write `n/a — D28-043: no client-side moderation`.
items.test:
Find the verdict (a boolean/score before the upload call). Two halves: (1) is the verdict a
request field — then set it from curl; (2) hook the classifier to return "safe" and upload a benign
test image the classifier normally blocks (use a harmless stand-in such as a known test pattern the
filter flags; never real abusive content). Does the server re-scan?
items.how:
```bash
grep -rnE 'isSafe|moderation|nsfwScore|safetyVerdict|classify\(' "$DEC/jadx/sources" | grep -vE '/(android|androidx)/' | head
# (1) the verdict in the body: mitmproxy ~b 'safe|moderation|score'  → flip from curl
# (2) hook: return the pass value from the classifier method, then perform the upload
cat > frida/mod-pass.js <<'JS'
Java.perform(function(){ var C=Java.use('<classifier class>'); C.<verdictMethod>.implementation=function(){ var r=this.<verdictMethod>.apply(this,arguments); console.log('[MOD] real='+r+' -> pass'); return <passValue>; }; });
JS
frida -D "$SERIAL" -n "$PKG" -l frida/mod-pass.js -t 5 | tee -a logs/D28-043.txt
```
items.proof:
The server accepting (201/visible to account B) an item the client classifier blocks,
with either the flipped request field or the hook log, and no server-side rejection after the fact
(check again at +10 min).
items.escalation:
A legal/policy gate → read the programme's abuse rules and file as the control's
bypass; verdicts that unlock money or entitlement → D28-044.
items.ruled_out_when:
The server re-scans and rejects or hides the item within the retention window
(the +10 min check from account B), and no verdict field exists in the request — record both.

items.title: Client-side AI decisions with money or entitlement outcomes trusted by the server — fraud score, OCR'd amount, credit limit, price, identity
items.severity_note: Critical
items.vrt: `broken_authentication_and_session_management.authentication_bypass` (P1) for identity/liveness verdicts; `broken_access_control.privilege_escalation` (varies) for a client-asserted score that unlocks a limit; the money node per D23 (client-computed price → D23-021)
items.attacker: AM-01 (the verdict or extracted value is a request field settable from curl); AM-12 only to find the field
items.applies_to: Apps where an on-device or client-called model produces a value the server consumes without recomputing: receipt/cheque OCR amounts, KYC match scores, fraud/risk scores, credit decisions, price or damage estimates
items.maps_to: D13-081 (KYC face match on the client), D15-082 (KYC/OCR fields asserted by the client), D23-021 (client-computed price), D23-005; MASWE-0023, MASWE-0050; CWE-602, CWE-807
items.skip_when: `inventory/ai.csv` has no feature whose consumer is `decide`/`bill` (D28-002) and no captured body carries a score/amount/verdict field; write `n/a — D28-044: no client-side AI verdict reaches the server`.
items.test:
Find the field (score, amount, `match`, `liveness`, `risk`) in the request after the model
runs. Replay with the value changed from curl (D15-082's method). Then the two-half rule (D23-005):
does the server recompute from the raw image/data it also receives, or does it store the client's
number?
items.how:
```bash
# mitmproxy ~b 'score|amount|liveness|match|risk|confidence' on the post-inference request → E-NNN
jq '.amount = 0.01' body.json > body-amt.json; jq '.liveness.score = 0.99 | .liveness.passed = true' body.json > body-live.json
for b in amt live; do curl -sS -o "responses/E-NNN-$b.http" -w "$b HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST "$URL" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data "@body-$b.json"; done | tee -a logs/D28-044.txt
# then read the state back (balance, verification status, order total) from a GET
```
items.proof:
The server-side state (verification status, credited amount, approved limit, order total)
reflecting the client-asserted value, read back after the modified request — with the raw input
unchanged.
items.escalation:
Identity → D13-081 at P1; money → D23-021/D23-025 with the settlement shown; a fraud
score that disables step-up → D13-070.
items.ruled_out_when:
The server ignores or recomputes the field (state unchanged across the two
replays, or `400`/`422` on the inconsistent value, with the raw data visibly re-scored) — record the
replays and the read-back.

items.title: Prompt templates, guardrails and tool allow-lists delivered by remote config or OTA with no signature — the model's control plane is attacker-writable
items.severity_note: High (the delivered template controls which tools fire or which rules apply); Critical when it adds a side-effect tool reachable from content (D28-024)

items.applies_to: Apps fetching `system_prompt`, `tools`, `safety`, `allowed_domains` or `agent_policy` values from remote config, a CMS, or an OTA bundle
items.maps_to: D17-037 (remote config as an unsigned security control plane), D18-025 (Remote Config as a trust boundary), D18-024 (values the device received), D17-027 (OTA bundle signature); MASWE-0011, MASWE-0049; CWE-345, CWE-494

items.test:
Capture the config/OTA response carrying the template or tool list; check what binds it
(signature in the package? a hash from the same response? TLS only?). Modify it with the proxy: add a
tool name from D28-005 to the allow-list, remove a guardrail line, repoint `allowed_domains`. Then run
D28-023's canary through the newly enabled tool.
items.how:
```bash
# mitmproxy ~b 'system_prompt|instructions|tools|allowed_domains|guardrail'  → E-NNN
grep -rnE 'RemoteConfig|getString\("(prompt|system|tools)|FirebaseRemoteConfig|ConfigFetch' "$DEC/jadx/sources" | grep -vE '/androidx/' | head
# map_local the modified response; then D28-024's dispatcher hook to show the added tool is now callable
frida -D "$SERIAL" -n "$PKG" -l frida/tool-dispatch.js -t 5 | tee -a logs/D28-045.txt
```
items.proof:
The dispatcher log showing a tool enabled only by the modified config executing from
content, or the guardrail-free template in the next model request — with the transport binding shown
absent (no signature verification class on the path).
items.escalation:
→ D28-024 at the tool's node under AM-09; → D17-037 for the generic control-plane
rating; a cleartext or unpinned fetch → D14 for the AM-06 upgrade.
items.ruled_out_when:
The template/tool list is signed and verified against a key in the package
(class:line), or the tool allow-list is enforced in code regardless of config (the added name is
rejected by the dispatcher, class:line); record the rejection.

As A, create a thread with a canary; log out; log in as B; open the AI feature and the
history list; search for the canary in the UI and in the sandbox. Repeat with a work profile /

items.how:
```bash
adb -s "$SERIAL" shell 'uiautomator dump /sdcard/ui.xml && grep -c '"$CANARY"' /sdcard/ui.xml' | tee -a logs/D28-052.txt
adb -s "$SERIAL" shell 'run-as '"$PKG"' grep -rl '"$CANARY"' /data/data/'"$PKG" 2>/dev/null
```
items.proof:
A's canary visible in B's UI (screenshot) or still on disk after logout (path), on the
same device.
items.escalation: → D20-060 for the rating; a server-side history served to B → D28-014 at P3/P1.

Logout clears the transcript store (file list before/after) and the history view

Start the mode with a canary on screen; end the session; sweep the sandbox and the capture


items.title: Hallucinated URLs, package names or dependencies the app auto-opens, auto-installs or auto-fetches (in-app slopsquatting)
items.severity_note: Medium (the app opens or installs what the model invented and an attacker registered); Low when the user must tap through a visible URL
items.vrt: `unvalidated_redirects_and_forwards.open_redirect.get_based` (P4) for the open; `insecure_data_transport.executable_download.no_secure_integrity_check` (P4) for an auto-fetch of code or a model
items.attacker: AM-01 (registers the hallucinated host, package or package name)
items.applies_to: Assistants that suggest and then act: "open the app for this", "install the plugin", "download the model", link lists rendered as tappable with no domain check
items.maps_to: D28-025 (URL sink), D17-007 (ingress capability), D09-020 (dangling hosts); MASWE-0029; CWE-601, CWE-494; ATT&CK T1655
items.skip_when: D28-025 is n/a (no URL/launch consumer) and no install/download tool exists; write `n/a — D28-055: no act-on-suggestion path`.
items.test:
Ask the feature 20 times for links/apps/plugins in a niche the model tends to invent; collect
every host and package name it produces; check which are unregistered (`dig`, Play lookup); do not
register anything — the finding is the consumer (D28-025) with the measured hallucination rate as the
precondition.
items.how:
```bash
grep -oE 'https?://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+|[a-z]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+){2,}' logs/D28-055.txt | sort -u | while read -r h; do printf '%s %s\n' "$h" "$(dig +short "${h#*://}" | head -1)"; done
```
items.proof:
The rate of unregistered suggestions (n/20) plus D28-025's proof that the app opens or
fetches them without a domain check.
items.escalation: → D28-025 / D28-039 for the sink; an install path → D17-007.
items.ruled_out_when:
Suggested links are shown as text with the full URL and need a tap into the
browser (no in-app open), or an allow-list filters them (class:line).


`pocs/F-NNN/` holding `runs.log` (controls + ≥5 runs or n ≥ 10 with the rate), the
payload, `repro.sh`, and the video with the sentinel frames.
